_readme.purpose: Retrieval eval set for the fintech compliance KB. Scored on whether the expected source document appears in top-k, not on answer text.
_readme.verified: Questions marked verified:true are grounded in passages confirmed present in the corpus. Questions marked verified:false are plausible but UNCHECKED - read the source document and correct expected_doc/answer_note before trusting their scores.

questions.question: What is the maximum period a payment service provider has to respond to a complaint in exceptional circumstances beyond its control?
questions.answer_note: 35 business days. Confirmed present in Chapter 11.
questions.notes: Retrieved cleanly under jurisdiction=UK filter during baseline testing.

questions.question: Which version of the Payment Services and Electronic Money Approach Document is current, and when was it published?
questions.answer_note: Version 8, May 2026.
questions.notes: Tests whether version-control front matter is retrievable at all - front matter often chunks poorly.

questions.question: Which types of business is the FCA Approach Document aimed at?
questions.answer_note: Authorised and small payment institutions (PIs), authorised and small e-money institutions (EMIs), registered account information service providers (RAISPs), credit institutions, and firms under TPR, SRO and CRO.
questions.notes: List-heavy passage. Good test of whether bulleted lists survive chunking.

questions.question: Which sourcebooks contain the FCA rules on safeguarding and resolution packs?
questions.answer_note: CASS 10A and CASS 15. Safeguarding audits and monthly returns sit in SUP.
questions.notes: Acronym-heavy - a good candidate for testing hybrid vs pure semantic search.

questions.question: What is the Voluntary Jurisdiction and who can join it?
questions.answer_note: Referenced at 11.49 - firms, PSPs and e-money issuers can join the VJ.
questions.notes: Tests whether the abbreviation VJ retrieves when spelled out in the query.

questions.question: What must a financial firm do to acknowledge a complaint under ASIC's internal dispute resolution requirements?
questions.answer_note: RG 271.50 covers acknowledgement of complaints and IDR response timeliness.
questions.notes: Confirmed retrievable - appeared in unfiltered baseline testing.

questions.question: What time limits apply to non-superannuation complaints under the AFCA Rules?
questions.answer_note: RG 267.166-167 distinguish superannuation from non-superannuation complaint time limits.
questions.notes: Confirmed present. Note this is AFCA oversight, not firm-level IDR obligations.

questions.question: What are the strong customer authentication exemptions for contactless payments?
questions.answer_note: UNVERIFIED - Chapter 20 covers SCA exemptions including contactless. Read Ch.20 and fill in the actual thresholds.
questions.notes: Chapter confirmed from version-control table; specific content unchecked.

questions.question: What does the guidance say about terminating framework contracts?
questions.answer_note: UNVERIFIED - paragraph 8.98 referenced in version control. Read and confirm.
questions.notes: Tests retrieval of a specific numbered paragraph.

questions.question: What is the risk-based approach to payments introduced by the Payment Services (Amendment) Regulations 2024?
questions.answer_note: UNVERIFIED - FG24/6 is the finalised guidance on this. Chapter 8 of the Approach Document also covers it, so either doc may be acceptable.
questions.notes: Two documents cover this. Consider allowing either as correct.

questions.question: What are the FCA requirements for complaint handling timeframes?
questions.answer_note: Chapter 11. Includes the 35 business day exceptional-circumstances limit.
questions.notes: THE BASELINE QUESTION. Unfiltered: 4/5 results were RG 267 (AU). Filtered to UK: 3/3 correct.

questions.question: What are ASIC's requirements for internal dispute resolution timeframes?
questions.answer_note: RG 271 sets IDR response timeframes.
questions.notes: Mirror of Q11. Confirms filtering works in both directions, not just toward the larger corpus.

questions.question: What are the UK safeguarding requirements for customer funds held by an e-money institution?
questions.answer_note: VERIFIED doc. WARNING: rank-1 PASS on chunks about authorisation and internal controls, not safeguarding. Lowest scores in the set (0.49/0.47/0.42). Q21 pulls the actual 'How must funds be safeguarded?' passage at 0.618 from the same document, so the content is retrievable and this phrasing misses it. Document-level scoring cannot see this.
questions.notes: Both the Approach Document and PS25/12 are plausible. Decide which you consider correct.

questions.question: What are the Australian licensing requirements for a limited AFS licence?
questions.answer_note: UNVERIFIED - INFO 179 covers limited AFS licence applications.
questions.notes: Tests whether a short info sheet competes against longer regulatory guides.

questions.question: What does the FCA expect regarding operational resilience for cryptoasset firms?
questions.answer_note: UNVERIFIED - FG26/6 is Guidance on Cryptoasset Operational Resilience.
questions.notes: Should NOT return FG26/4 (Material Third Party Reporting) despite topical overlap.

questions.question: How does the Consumer Duty apply to cryptoasset firms?
questions.answer_note: UNVERIFIED - FG26/5 is Application of the Consumer Duty to Cryptoasset Firms.
questions.notes: Near-miss risk: FG26/6 and FG26/7 are also crypto guidance.

questions.question: What are the timeframes for responding to a customer complaint?
questions.answer_note: Both UK (Approach Doc Ch.11) and AU (RG 271) cover this with DIFFERENT requirements. Correct behaviour is to ask which jurisdiction, or answer for both with clear labelling.
questions.notes: Baseline: returned 2 chunks, both RG 271, zero UK. This is the contamination case.

questions.question: How long do we have to acknowledge receipt of a complaint?
questions.answer_note: BLOCKED: does the FCA Approach Document state a complaint ACKNOWLEDGEMENT timeframe, or only cross-refer to DISP? RG 271.51 is a clean AU hit. If the UK half is not in the corpus, reclassify as jurisdiction_specific AU.
questions.notes: Uses 'we' - the phrasing a real compliance officer would use, with no jurisdiction cue.

questions.question: What are our obligations when outsourcing a critical function to a third party?
questions.answer_note: UNVERIFIED - FG26/4 (UK, material third party reporting) and ASIC outsourcing expectations both plausible.
questions.notes: Check whether the AU corpus actually covers outsourcing before trusting this one.

questions.question: What must we do to become licensed before we can operate?
questions.answer_note: REWRITTEN - was 'obtain a licence to provide payment services'. 'Payment services' is a UK/EU term of art with no AU counterpart, so the original could only ever return UK. AU licensing content exists (RG 207, RG 112, INFO-179, ASIC-Licensing-Admin) so the reworded form is genuinely cross-jurisdiction. UNVERIFIED until re-run.
questions.notes: High-value bait: a wrong answer here would be a serious real-world error.

questions.question: How must customer funds be safeguarded?
questions.answer_note: RECLASSIFIED from cross_jurisdiction_bait. The AU corpus has no client-money/safeguarding guide, so returning UK only is correct, not a failure.
questions.notes: May need reclassifying after checking AU coverage.

questions.question: What are the rules on conduct when dealing with retail customers?
questions.answer_note: UNVERIFIED - multiple documents on both sides tagged topic_conduct.
questions.notes: Deliberately vague. Tests whether the system asks for scope rather than guessing.

questions.question: Which chapters of the Approach Document were changed by the May 2026 safeguarding updates, and what do those changes cover?
questions.answer_note: BLOCKED: does the Approach Document list which chapters the May 2026 safeguarding updates changed? Retrieval returned version-history front matter; the only plausibly useful chunk was ps25-12 at rank 5. If no such list exists, rewrite or drop.
questions.notes: Answer spans front matter plus body. Tests whether retrieval can assemble across distant chunks.

questions.question: How do the FCA and ASIC complaint response timeframes differ?
questions.answer_note: VERIFIED. Currently FAILS: returns RG 267 (AFCA oversight) not RG 271 (firm IDR obligations), and zero UK chunks. Same wrong-obligation drift seen in the Aurora baseline. Keep failing - this is the target failure mode.
questions.notes: The comparison question a real user would ask. Needs both jurisdictions retrieved deliberately, not accidentally.

questions.question: What changed between version 6 and version 8 of the Approach Document?
questions.answer_note: BLOCKED: does the Approach Document contain a v6-to-v8 changelog? Retrieval returned the paragraph about the FIFTH version. Scored rank-1 PASS purely on filename. If no changelog exists, rewrite or drop.
questions.notes: Tests temporal reasoning over a table.

questions.question: If a firm operates under the temporary permissions regime, which parts of the payment services rules apply to it?
questions.answer_note: UNVERIFIED - TPR mentioned in preface; Chapter 6 covers it per version control notes.
questions.notes: Requires linking the preface's audience list to the substantive chapter.

questions.question: What are the Monetary Authority of Singapore's requirements for payment institution licensing?
questions.answer_note: The corpus contains no MAS material. Correct behaviour is to refuse and say so.
questions.notes: Tests refusal. A UK or AU answer here is a failure, not a partial success.

questions.question: What is the maximum penalty for breaching safeguarding requirements?
questions.answer_note: UNVERIFIED as strictly absent, but the corpus is guidance rather than enforcement material - penalties are unlikely to be covered. Confirm before scoring.
questions.notes: Plausible-sounding but probably outside the corpus. Check before trusting.

questions.question: How many payment institutions were authorised by the FCA in 2025?
questions.answer_note: Statistical data, not present in guidance documents. Correct behaviour is refusal.
questions.notes: Tests whether the system invents plausible numbers.

questions.question: What are the FCA's requirements for cryptoasset custody wallets under the proposed 2027 regime?
questions.answer_note: Fictional future regime. The corpus has crypto guidance (FG26/5, 6, 7) which will look topically relevant - that is the trap.
questions.notes: Hardest refusal case: topically adjacent content exists and will retrieve with decent scores.
